tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label and message are the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

# CLAUDE.md - Testing Guide for OrcaSlicer

This guide provides comprehensive instructions for Claude Code when writing, maintaining, and understanding tests in the OrcaSlicer codebase.

## ⚠️ CRITICAL RULES - MUST FOLLOW

### 1. **SECTIONS IN LOOPS - NEVER REUSE NAMES**
❌ **WRONG**: Will cause unpredictable behavior
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Bad loop sections") {
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        SECTION("Same name") {  // WRONG! Same name used multiple times
            REQUIRE(i >= 0);
        }
    }
}
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Use DYNAMIC_SECTION or incorporate counter
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Good loop sections") {
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        DYNAMIC_SECTION("Section " << i) {  // Unique name per iteration
            REQUIRE(i >= 0);
        }
    }
}
```

### 2. **THREAD SAFETY - ASSERTIONS ARE NOT THREAD-SAFE**
❌ **WRONG**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Multi-threaded test") {
    std::vector<std::thread> threads;
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        threads.emplace_back([]() {
            REQUIRE(some_calculation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
        });
    }
}
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Synchronize results, test on main thread
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Multi-threaded test") {
    std::vector<std::thread> threads;
    std::atomic<int> passed{0};
    
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        threads.emplace_back([&passed]() {
            if (some_calculation() == expected) {
                passed++;
            }
        });
    }
    
    for (auto& t : threads) t.join();
    REQUIRE(passed == 4);  // Test results on main thread
}
```

### 3. **EXPRESSION DECOMPOSITION - AVOID BINARY OPERATORS**
❌ **WRONG**: Cannot decompose properly
```cpp
REQUIRE(a > 0 && b < 10);  // Shows "false" on failure, not individual values
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Split into separate assertions
```cpp
REQUIRE(a > 0);
REQUIRE(b < 10);  // Each shows individual values on failure
```

### 4. **FLOATING POINT - NEVER USE APPROX**
❌ **WRONG**: Approx is deprecated and asymmetric
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_value == Catch::Approx(expected));  // Deprecated!
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Use floating point matchers
```cpp
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinAbs(expected, 0.001));
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinRel(expected, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinULP(expected, 4));     // 4 ULPs apart
```

### 5. **TEST ORDERING - ALWAYS USE RANDOM ORDER**
✅ **REQUIRED**: For CI/CD and development
```bash
# Essential flags for running tests
./tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions

# For test sharding (parallel execution), share random seed
./tests --order rand --shard-index 0 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
./tests --order rand --shard-index 1 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
./tests --order rand --shard-index 2 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
```

## Overview of OrcaSlicer's Testing Framework

OrcaSlicer uses **Catch2 v3** (currently v3.11.0, vendored in `tests/catch2/`) as its primary testing framework. The test suite is organized into several modules that mirror the project's architectural components:

> **Note**: Test files include the framework via `#include <catch2/catch_all.hpp>` (the v3 single-header convenience include). All v3 features described in this guide are available.

### Test Structure
```
tests/
├── CMakeLists.txt              # Main test configuration
├── catch_main.hpp              # Custom test reporter
├── libslic3r/                  # Core library tests (21 test files)
├── fff_print/                  # FFF printing tests (12 test files)
├── sla_print/                  # SLA printing tests (4 test files)
├── libnest2d/                  # 2D nesting tests
├── slic3rutils/               # Utility tests
├── data/                      # Test data files and meshes
└── catch2/                    # Catch2 framework files
```

### Build Integration
- Tests are built using CMake with `catch_discover_tests()` integration
- Each test module creates a separate executable (e.g., `libslic3r_tests`, `fff_print_tests`)
- Test data directory is available via `TEST_DATA_DIR` preprocessor definition
- Custom verbose console reporter provides detailed test output

## Test Suite Organization

### libslic3r Tests
Core slicing engine tests covering:
- **Geometry operations**: Points, polygons, lines, Voronoi diagrams
- **File formats**: STL, 3MF, AMF parsing and validation
- **Algorithms**: Clipper operations, mesh boolean operations, optimization
- **Configuration**: Print settings validation and parsing
- **Utilities**: String processing, time utilities, data structures

### fff_print Tests
Fused Filament Fabrication specific tests:
- **G-code generation**: Writer functionality, cooling, lift/unlift
- **Slicing algorithms**: Layer generation, infill patterns
- **Print mechanics**: Flow calculations, extrusion, support material
- **Model processing**: Print objects, skirt/brim generation

### sla_print Tests
Stereolithography specific tests:
- **SLA print processing**: Layer curing, support generation
- **Raycast operations**: Light path calculations
- **Test utilities**: SLA-specific helper functions

## Writing New Tests - Best Practices

### File Organization
1. **Naming Convention**: `test_<feature>.cpp` (e.g., `test_geometry.cpp`)
2. **Header Structure**: Include `<catch2/catch_all.hpp>` first, then relevant headers
3. **Namespace Usage**: Use `using namespace Slic3r;` for convenience
4. **File Placement**: Add to appropriate test directory and update CMakeLists.txt

### Test Naming and Structure
```cpp
#include <catch2/catch_all.hpp>
#include "libslic3r/Point.hpp"

using namespace Slic3r;

TEST_CASE("Feature description", "[category_tag]") {
    // Test implementation
}
```

### Tagging System
Use descriptive tags for test categorization:
- `[Geometry]` - Geometric operations and calculations
- `[GCodeWriter]` - G-code generation functionality  
- `[Config]` - Configuration and settings tests
- `[FileFormat]` - File I/O operations (STL, 3MF, etc.)
- `[Algorithm]` - Core algorithms and processing
- `[Performance]` - Performance benchmarks (if applicable)

## Catch2 Features Guide

### Basic Assertions
```cpp
// Primary assertions - stop test on failure
REQUIRE(expression);
REQUIRE_FALSE(expression);

// Continuing assertions - continue test after failure  
CHECK(expression);
CHECK_FALSE(expression);

// Non-failing checks - record result but don't fail test
CHECK_NOFAIL(expression);  // Useful for assumptions that might be violated
```

### Exception Testing
```cpp
// Verify no exception is thrown

## Common Pitfalls and Solutions

### Floating-Point Comparisons

> **CRITICAL**: Never use Approx - it's deprecated due to asymmetry and other issues

❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == expected_volume);           // Exact equality
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == Catch::Approx(expected));   // Deprecated! Asymmetric!
```

✅ **Correct**: Always use floating point matchers
```cpp
// Absolute tolerance - good when values are near zero
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinAbs(expected_volume, 0.001));

// Relative tolerance - good for values with different magnitudes
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance

// ULP (Units in Last Place) - most precise, requires IEEE-754
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinULP(expected_volume, 4));

// Combined approach - relative OR absolute
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, 
    WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.001) || WithinAbs(0.0, 0.000001));

// Precision control for output
Catch::StringMaker<double>::precision = 15;  // Show more decimal places
```

### Why Approx is Problematic:
- **Asymmetric**: `Approx(10).epsilon(0.1) != 11.1` but `Approx(11.1).epsilon(0.1) == 10`
- **Double-only**: All computation done in `double`, causes issues with `float` inputs  
- **Default behavior**: Only uses relative comparison, so `Approx(0) == X` only works for `X == 0`

### Path Handling
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
std::string path = TEST_DATA_DIR + "/model.obj";  // May have path separator issues
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
std::string path = std::string(TEST_DATA_DIR) + "/model.obj";
// or use boost::filesystem for complex path operations
```

### Exception Testing
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
bool threw_exception = false;
try {
    risky_function();
} catch (...) {
    threw_exception = true;
}
REQUIRE(threw_exception);
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
REQUIRE_THROWS(risky_function());
// or for specific exceptions
REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(risky_function(), SpecificException);
```

### Thread Safety

⚠️ **CRITICAL**: Catch2 assertions are **NOT thread-safe** by default!

> **Note**: Catch2 v3.9.0+ has opt-in thread-safe assertions via `CATCH_CONFIG_EXPERIMENTAL_THREAD_SAFE_ASSERTIONS`. OrcaSlicer is on v3.11.0 but does not enable this flag, so assertions remain non-thread-safe by default.

❌ **Incorrect**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
std::thread t([&]() {
    REQUIRE(threaded_operation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
    CHECK(other_operation());                   // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
});
```

✅ **Correct**: Collect results, assert on main thread
```cpp
std::atomic<bool> success{false};
std::atomic<int> error_count{0};

std::thread t([&]() {
    // Do work in thread, collect results
    bool result1 = (threaded_operation() == expected);
    bool result2 = other_operation();
    
    if (result1 && result2) {
        success = true;
    } else {
        error_count++;
    }
});

t.join();

// Assert results on main thread
REQUIRE(success);
REQUIRE(error_count == 0);
```

#### Thread Safety Rules:
- **REQUIRE family**: Would terminate process in spawned threads (throws exception with no try-catch)
- **CHECK family**: Not thread-safe, can corrupt internal state
- **SKIP, FAIL, SUCCEED**: Not thread-safe even with v3 thread-safe assertions
- **Message macros**: INFO, CAPTURE, WARN - not thread-safe
- **STATIC_REQUIRE/CHECK**: Not thread-safe (relies on runtime registration)

# CLAUDE.md - Testing Guide for OrcaSlicer

This guide provides comprehensive instructions for Claude Code when writing, maintaining, and understanding tests in the OrcaSlicer codebase.

## ⚠️ CRITICAL RULES - MUST FOLLOW

### 1. **SECTIONS IN LOOPS - NEVER REUSE NAMES**
❌ **WRONG**: Will cause unpredictable behavior
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Bad loop sections") {
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        SECTION("Same name") {  // WRONG! Same name used multiple times
            REQUIRE(i >= 0);
        }
    }
}
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Use DYNAMIC_SECTION or incorporate counter
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Good loop sections") {
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        DYNAMIC_SECTION("Section " << i) {  // Unique name per iteration
            REQUIRE(i >= 0);
        }
    }
}
```

### 2. **THREAD SAFETY - ASSERTIONS ARE NOT THREAD-SAFE**
❌ **WRONG**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Multi-threaded test") {
    std::vector<std::thread> threads;
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        threads.emplace_back([]() {
            REQUIRE(some_calculation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
        });
    }
}
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Synchronize results, test on main thread
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Multi-threaded test") {
    std::vector<std::thread> threads;
    std::atomic<int> passed{0};
    
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        threads.emplace_back([&passed]() {
            if (some_calculation() == expected) {
                passed++;
            }
        });
    }
    
    for (auto& t : threads) t.join();
    REQUIRE(passed == 4);  // Test results on main thread
}
```

### 3. **EXPRESSION DECOMPOSITION - AVOID BINARY OPERATORS**
❌ **WRONG**: Cannot decompose properly
```cpp
REQUIRE(a > 0 && b < 10);  // Shows "false" on failure, not individual values
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Split into separate assertions
```cpp
REQUIRE(a > 0);
REQUIRE(b < 10);  // Each shows individual values on failure
```

### 4. **FLOATING POINT - NEVER USE APPROX**
❌ **WRONG**: Approx is deprecated and asymmetric
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_value == Catch::Approx(expected));  // Deprecated!
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Use floating point matchers
```cpp
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinAbs(expected, 0.001));
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinRel(expected, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinULP(expected, 4));     // 4 ULPs apart
```

### 5. **TEST ORDERING - ALWAYS USE RANDOM ORDER**
✅ **REQUIRED**: For CI/CD and development
```bash
# Essential flags for running tests
./tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions

# For test sharding (parallel execution), share random seed
./tests --order rand --shard-index 0 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
./tests --order rand --shard-index 1 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
./tests --order rand --shard-index 2 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
```

## Overview of OrcaSlicer's Testing Framework

OrcaSlicer uses **Catch2 v3** (currently v3.11.0, vendored in `tests/catch2/`) as its primary testing framework. The test suite is organized into several modules that mirror the project's architectural components:

> **Note**: Test files include the framework via `#include <catch2/catch_all.hpp>` (the v3 single-header convenience include). All v3 features described in this guide are available.

### Test Structure
```
tests/
├── CMakeLists.txt              # Main test configuration
├── catch_main.hpp              # Custom test reporter
├── libslic3r/                  # Core library tests (21 test files)
├── fff_print/                  # FFF printing tests (12 test files)
├── sla_print/                  # SLA printing tests (4 test files)
├── libnest2d/                  # 2D nesting tests
├── slic3rutils/               # Utility tests
├── data/                      # Test data files and meshes
└── catch2/                    # Catch2 framework files
```

### Build Integration
- Tests are built using CMake with `catch_discover_tests()` integration
- Each test module creates a separate executable (e.g., `libslic3r_tests`, `fff_print_tests`)
- Test data directory is available via `TEST_DATA_DIR` preprocessor definition
- Custom verbose console reporter provides detailed test output

## Writing New Tests - Best Practices

### File Organization
1. **Naming Convention**: `test_<feature>.cpp` (e.g., `test_geometry.cpp`)
2. **Header Structure**: Include `<catch2/catch_all.hpp>` first, then relevant headers
3. **Namespace Usage**: Use `using namespace Slic3r;` for convenience
4. **File Placement**: Add to appropriate test directory and update CMakeLists.txt

### Test Naming and Structure
```cpp
#include <catch2/catch_all.hpp>
#include "libslic3r/Point.hpp"

using namespace Slic3r;

TEST_CASE("Feature description", "[category_tag]") {
    // Test implementation
}
```

### Tagging System
Use descriptive tags for test categorization:
- `[Geometry]` - Geometric operations and calculations
- `[GCodeWriter]` - G-code generation functionality

### Basic Assertions
```cpp
// Primary assertions - stop test on failure
REQUIRE(expression);
REQUIRE_FALSE(expression);

// Continuing assertions - continue test after failure  
CHECK(expression);
CHECK_FALSE(expression);

// Non-failing checks - record result but don't fail test
CHECK_NOFAIL(expression);  // Useful for assumptions that might be violated
```

### Exception Testing
```cpp

REQUIRE_NOTHROW(function_call());

// Verify any exception is thrown
REQUIRE_THROWS(risky_function());

// Verify specific exception type
REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(function_call(), SpecificException);

// Verify exception message
REQUIRE_THROWS_WITH(function_call(), "Expected error message");

// Verify exception with matchers (for partial matching)

                       Catch::Matchers::Message("contains this"));

### Complex Assertions with Matchers
```cpp

// String matchers
using Catch::Matchers::StartsWith;
using Catch::Matchers::EndsWith;
using Catch::Matchers::ContainsSubstring;
using Catch::Matchers::Equals;
using Catch::Matchers::Matches;  // Regex matching

REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, ContainsSubstring("middle part"));
REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, Matches(".*pattern.*"));

using Catch::Matchers::WithinRel;
using Catch::Matchers::WithinULP;

REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinAbs(expected, 0.001));     // Absolute tolerance
REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinRel(expected, 0.01));      // Relative tolerance (1%)
REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinULP(expected, 4));         // ULP difference (requires IEEE-754)

// Combining matchers

## Common Pitfalls and Solutions

### Floating-Point Comparisons

> **CRITICAL**: Never use Approx - it's deprecated due to asymmetry and other issues

❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == expected_volume);           // Exact equality
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == Catch::Approx(expected));   // Deprecated! Asymmetric!
```

✅ **Correct**: Always use floating point matchers
```cpp
// Absolute tolerance - good when values are near zero
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinAbs(expected_volume, 0.001));

// Relative tolerance - good for values with different magnitudes
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance

// ULP (Units in Last Place) - most precise, requires IEEE-754
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinULP(expected_volume, 4));

// Combined approach - relative OR absolute
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, 
    WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.001) || WithinAbs(0.0, 0.000001));

// Precision control for output
Catch::StringMaker<double>::precision = 15;  // Show more decimal places
```

### Why Approx is Problematic:
- **Asymmetric**: `Approx(10).epsilon(0.1) != 11.1` but `Approx(11.1).epsilon(0.1) == 10`
- **Double-only**: All computation done in `double`, causes issues with `float` inputs  
- **Default behavior**: Only uses relative comparison, so `Approx(0) == X` only works for `X == 0`

### Path Handling
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
std::string path = TEST_DATA_DIR + "/model.obj";  // May have path separator issues
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
std::string path = std::string(TEST_DATA_DIR) + "/model.obj";
// or use boost::filesystem for complex path operations
```

### Exception Testing
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
bool threw_exception = false;
try {
    risky_function();
} catch (...) {
    threw_exception = true;
}
REQUIRE(threw_exception);
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp

// or for specific exceptions
REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(risky_function(), SpecificException);
```

### Thread Safety

⚠️ **CRITICAL**: Catch2 assertions are **NOT thread-safe** by default!

> **Note**: Catch2 v3.9.0+ has opt-in thread-safe assertions via `CATCH_CONFIG_EXPERIMENTAL_THREAD_SAFE_ASSERTIONS`. OrcaSlicer is on v3.11.0 but does not enable this flag, so assertions remain non-thread-safe by default.

❌ **Incorrect**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
std::thread t([&]() {
    REQUIRE(threaded_operation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
    CHECK(other_operation());                   // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
});
```

✅ **Correct**: Collect results, assert on main thread
```cpp
std::atomic<bool> success{false};
std::atomic<int> error_count{0};

std::thread t([&]() {
    // Do work in thread, collect results
    bool result1 = (threaded_operation() == expected);
    bool result2 = other_operation();
    
    if (result1 && result2) {
        success = true;
    } else {
        error_count++;

- **REQUIRE family**: Would terminate process in spawned threads (throws exception with no try-catch)
- **CHECK family**: Not thread-safe, can corrupt internal state
- **SKIP, FAIL, SUCCEED**: Not thread-safe even with v3 thread-safe assertions
- **Message macros**: INFO, CAPTURE, WARN - not thread-safe
- **STATIC_REQUIRE/CHECK**: Not thread-safe (relies on runtime registration)

Send every chat from an append-only record of what it sent

Provider prompt caches (Anthropic and OpenAI) only reuse the part of a
request that opens with exactly the bytes of an earlier one. The host used
to rebuild a chat's earlier turns for every request in a shorter form:
plain text, calls replayed without the thinking around them, workspace
blocks and pictures stripped, skills dropped. So the start of the history
changed on every turn, and every turn paid full price for all of it.

Now each chat keeps a record in the project document of every item the
model was sent, and every request is that record followed by what the turn
has added so far:

- the person's messages, each with its print-issue context, workspace
  block, attachment listing, and picture or PDF parts as first sent; a
  file-load report as the turn's own words;
- the model's output exactly as the provider returned it, thinking or
  reasoning included (Responses items keep their ids);
- tool results in their own channel, pictures included;
- fired skills (their picture, then their text in the operator role) and
  the printer chat's notes as operator messages.

Items are only appended, never edited. ProviderAgent hands the host the
items a later request can follow on from: the person's side once a request
carrying it was accepted, each response with its results once the next
request went, the end of the turn when it completes. A trailing operator
message or a call without its result is never recorded. Picture and PDF
bytes go to blobs under attachments/chat-<id>/ beside the attachment
blobs; the document stores only their paths, and a reopened project reads
them back, so it renders the same bytes. Deleting a chat removes its blob
directory. A record is bound to the wire format it was written in; giving
it to the other format is a logic error (the model switch is refused
earlier in a following commit).

What an old chat's model now sees: a chat that talked before this change
gets a record the first time it talks again, once. It holds the person's
messages and file-load reports up to the last reply, and the replies, as
plain text. Its earlier tool calls and results, workspace blocks, pictures,
skills and notes were never kept and are not made up, so the model no
longer sees the earlier calls it used to get replayed. Messages after that
last reply go as any unsent message does.

Other differences in what the model sees:
- Skills stay in the record where they fired, on both formats (they used
  to be sent once on Responses, and kept within one turn only on
  Anthropic). A following commit makes Anthropic clear them.
- Earlier workspace blocks, pictures, attachments, and tool results with
  their workspace stay in later requests.
- An earlier tool result is now sent as Anthropic tool_result content
  blocks, the same as within a turn, instead of a plain string.
- A stopped or failed response's partial text and calls are not sent
  again; a message whose turn never reached the model still is.
- A title request sends the person's words only, without the chat.
- A retry whose turn the record already holds sends no new workspace.

Deleted: the host's history rebuild (its calls_by_message replay, the
retelling of reports and notes, the workspace and skill stripping), the
transcript's opening/user_content/steps split and the codecs' separate
paths for them, and tool_output_json, which only existed to share code
with the replay.

changed) is meant for the request that fired it. With the chat record

  through it skills stay visible, as they do on Responses, which has no
  such message.

  a clearing system message with one that stays, judges a run of system

  the assistant's), and still turns a run placed anywhere else into user
  text. Cache breakpoints go on user content only, never on a turn-scoped
  message.

  their texts, so a note is not split from the skill by a user message
  (which would turn the note into user text).

is no longer shown; through the gateway and on Responses it still is.

was made.

  texts.

  so PrinterConversation and PrinterPanel no longer set it.

preset's receipt rewrites that note and starts a turn on it. With the
record, the note counted as sent and the turn told the model nothing. A
note rewritten since the record holds it now goes again, as it reads now.
The receipt test proves it fails without the check.

What the model sees: no prefix; notes in the operator's voice; the
project chat's notes, which it did not see before. On Anthropic a note
with nothing from the person before it (a printer chat's turn the app
started) is still turned into user text, which the API requires.

Follow-up outside this change: tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp's
CalibrationAgent recognises app turns by the old prefix in user_text and
must read request.note instead.

Refuse a model in another wire format for a chat that has talked

A chat's record is kept in the wire format it was sent in (Anthropic
Messages or OpenAI Responses), and every later request sends it again as
it is, so a model in the other format cannot read it. Before this, a
person could pick such a model mid-chat, and the turn loop would then
throw on the mismatch.

- set_chat_model on a chat whose record has a format refuses a choice in
  another format: the chat keeps its model, the page gets the chat's
  choice back (its picker resets) and a bridge_error "chat_format_fixed"
  saying to start a new chat. Another model or thinking level in the same
  format goes, and a chat that has sent nothing takes any model.
- It also refuses JusPrin's gateway for a chat whose record holds a skill
  that clears (sent straight to Anthropic with clear_at): the gateway
  cannot pass the beta header that field needs.
- An account model whose format the account's list has not named yet is
  checked again when the chat next sends.
- When a turn starts, the same check runs on the chat's current choice,
  which can change under it (a provider whose key is gone leaves its chats
  on the default). The turn then fails with the same message instead of
  reaching the loop's logic error.

Not done: the page shows a bridge_error only as a diagnostic, so the
person sees the picker go back without the reason. Showing it is the
page's follow-up.

record, the note counted as sent and the turn told the model nothing. A
note rewritten since the record holds it now goes again, as it reads now.
The receipt test proves it fails without the check.

What the model sees: no prefix; notes in the operator's voice; the
project chat's notes, which it did not see before. On Anthropic a note
with nothing from the person before it (a printer chat's turn the app
started) is still turned into user text, which the API requires.

Follow-up outside this change: tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp's
CalibrationAgent recognises app turns by the old prefix in user_text and
must read request.note instead.

settling of an app turn's workspace with its note.

Refuse a model in another wire format for a chat that has talked

A chat's record is kept in the wire format it was sent in (Anthropic
Messages or OpenAI Responses), and every later request sends it again as
it is, so a model in the other format cannot read it. Before this, a
person could pick such a model mid-chat, and the turn loop would then
throw on the mismatch.

- set_chat_model on a chat whose record has a format refuses a choice in
  another format: the chat keeps its model, the page gets the chat's
  choice back (its picker resets) and a bridge_error "chat_format_fixed"
  saying to start a new chat. Another model or thinking level in the same
  format goes, and a chat that has sent nothing takes any model.
- It also refuses JusPrin's gateway for a chat whose record holds a skill
  that clears (sent straight to Anthropic with clear_at): the gateway
  cannot pass the beta header that field needs.
- An account model whose format the account's list has not named yet is
  checked again when the chat next sends.
- When a turn starts, the same check runs on the chat's current choice,
  which can change under it (a provider whose key is gone leaves its chats
  on the default). The turn then fails with the same message instead of
  reaching the loop's logic error.

Not done: the page shows a bridge_error only as a diagnostic, so the
person sees the picker go back without the reason. Showing it is the
page's follow-up.

Production diff: +38/-0, all of it the refusal and where it is checked.

# R7: every chat sends an append-only record of what it sent

Branch `claude/cache-r7-record-e80b27`, five commits on `0807d77282`, not pushed or merged.
Each request a chat sends now starts with the exact bytes of its previous request, so the
provider's prompt cache can reuse the earlier part on both Anthropic Messages and OpenAI
Responses. The agent suite passes (16777 assertions in 479 test cases, random order), and the
two history-prefix guard cases now run by default and pass on both wire formats.

| Commit | What |
|---|---|
| `ba08e2c18f` | R7: the per-chat record replaces the rebuilt history |
| `fe70eea593` | R2: a fired skill clears at the next user message on Anthropic (not through the gateway) |
| `f5039d09e8` | R6: app notes are operator messages in project and printer chats |
| `59304a1ef9` | D5: a chat that has talked refuses a model in the other wire format |
| `9fce6ddb2b` | The `[history-prefix]` guard runs by default (test-only) |

No live model calls were made. Everything below was checked with fake transports only.

## Design as built

**The record.** `ProjectStateDocument` keeps a `ChatRecord {format, items}` per chat. `format`
is `"anthropic"` or `"responses"` and is fixed by the first append. Each `RecordItem` is one of:

- `User`: the person's message as sent (words, print-issue context, workspace block, attachment
  listing, pictures and PDFs as parts). `source` is the message id.
- `Operator`: a fired skill's text or an app note. `clears` is set on skills that the provider
  can hide later (R2).
- `Assistant`: the provider's output item exactly as returned, thinking/reasoning included;
  Responses items keep their ids.
- `Results`: tool results, in the tool-result channel, pictures included.

Items are only appended. `append_chat_record` checks the format and builds all entries before
changing anything, so a bad append leaves the record untouched. Picture and PDF bytes are written
as blobs under `attachments/chat-<id>/<request_id>-<n>`; state.json holds only the paths, and a
reopened project reads the same bytes back. Deleting a chat removes that directory.

**When items are kept.** `ProviderAgent` reports items through `AgentRequest::on_recorded` only
once a later request can safely follow on from them:

- the person's side, once a request carrying it was accepted;
- a response and its results, once the next request was posted;
- the final response, when the turn completes.

A trailing operator item (skill or note) is kept only once a response follows it, and a call is
never kept without its result. In a turn the app starts with a note, the turn's workspace block
and the note are kept together after the model answers, so a failed request leaves neither
behind.

**Request order.** Each request is built as:

1. the record;
2. person messages not yet sent;
3. the turn's own user item (an empty-worded workspace item in an app turn);
4. fired skills' pictures;
5. notes (unsent ones, then the turn's note);
6. fired skills' texts.

A retry of a turn the record already holds adds no new workspace block. A record given to the
other wire format throws `logic_error`; D5 stops that from being reachable.

**Codecs.** Both codecs now render one list of record items instead of the old
opening/user_content/steps split.

- Anthropic: operator items become system messages in the conversation. Clearing ones carry
  `clear_at: "next_user_message"` and the request carries `anthropic-beta:
  mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21`. A clearing and a non-clearing system message
  are never merged. A run of system messages is judged together for placement (after a user
  message, and last or before the assistant's); any run placed elsewhere becomes user text. The
  moving cache breakpoint stays on the newest user message and never goes on a turn-scoped
  system message.
- Responses: operator items become `developer` items, assistant output is inserted verbatim,
  and results become `function_call_output` items followed by user picture messages.

**Skills clear per profile, never per request.** `clears_skills(profile)` is true for the
Anthropic family unless the profile is `account_sign_in` (JusPrin's gateway).

**D5.** `handle_set_chat_model` refuses a model whose format differs from the record's, and
refuses the gateway for a chat whose record has clearing skills. The chat keeps its model, the
page gets its unchanged choice back, and a `bridge_error` with code `chat_format_fixed` says to
start a new chat. A chat with no record takes any model. The same check runs when a turn starts,
because a chat's choice can change under it (for example a provider's key is removed). In that
case the turn fails with the same message.

## Migration of chats from before this change

A chat that talked before this change gets a record the first time it talks again, once. The

## Design as built

**The record.** `ProjectStateDocument` keeps a `ChatRecord {format, items}` per chat. `format`

- `Results`: tool results, in the tool-result channel, pictures included.

changing anything, so a bad append leaves the record untouched. Picture and PDF bytes are written

reopened project reads the same bytes back. Deleting a chat removes that directory.

once a later request can safely follow on from them:

- the person's side, once a request carrying it was accepted;
- a response and its results, once the next request was posted;
- the final response, when the turn completes.

and the note are kept together after the model answers, so a failed request leaves neither

2. person messages not yet sent;

other wire format throws `logic_error`; D5 stops that from being reachable.

# R7: every chat sends an append-only record of what it sent

Branch `claude/cache-r7-record-e80b27`, five commits on `0807d77282`, not pushed or merged.
Each request a chat sends now starts with the exact bytes of its previous request, so the
provider's prompt cache can reuse the earlier part on both Anthropic Messages and OpenAI
Responses. The agent suite passes (16777 assertions in 479 test cases, random order), and the
two history-prefix guard cases now run by default and pass on both wire formats.

| Commit | What |
|---|---|
| `ba08e2c18f` | R7: the per-chat record replaces the rebuilt history |
| `fe70eea593` | R2: a fired skill clears at the next user message on Anthropic (not through the gateway) |
| `f5039d09e8` | R6: app notes are operator messages in project and printer chats |
| `59304a1ef9` | D5: a chat that has talked refuses a model in the other wire format |
| `9fce6ddb2b` | The `[history-prefix]` guard runs by default (test-only) |

No live model calls were made. Everything below was checked with fake transports only.

## Design as built

**The record.** `ProjectStateDocument` keeps a `ChatRecord {format, items}` per chat. `format`
is `"anthropic"` or `"responses"` and is fixed by the first append. Each `RecordItem` is one of:

- `User`: the person's message as sent (words, print-issue context, workspace block, attachment
  listing, pictures and PDFs as parts). `source` is the message id.
- `Operator`: a fired skill's text or an app note. `clears` is set on skills that the provider
  can hide later (R2).
- `Assistant`: the provider's output item exactly as returned, thinking/reasoning included;
  Responses items keep their ids.
- `Results`: tool results, in the tool-result channel, pictures included.

Items are only appended. `append_chat_record` checks the format and builds all entries before
changing anything, so a bad append leaves the record untouched. Picture and PDF bytes are written
as blobs under `attachments/chat-<id>/<request_id>-<n>`; state.json holds only the paths, and a
reopened project reads the same bytes back. Deleting a chat removes that directory.

**When items are kept.** `ProviderAgent` reports items through `AgentRequest::on_recorded` only
once a later request can safely follow on from them:

- the person's side, once a request carrying it was accepted;
- a response and its results, once the next request was posted;
- the final response, when the turn completes.

A trailing operator item (skill or note) is kept only once a response follows it, and a call is
never kept without its result. In a turn the app starts with a note, the turn's workspace block
and the note are kept together after the model answers, so a failed request leaves neither
behind.

**Request order.** Each request is built as:

1. the record;
2. person messages not yet sent;
3. the turn's own user item (an empty-worded workspace item in an app turn);
4. fired skills' pictures;
5. notes (unsent ones, then the turn's note);
6. fired skills' texts.

A retry of a turn the record already holds adds no new workspace block. A record given to the
other wire format throws `logic_error`; D5 stops that from being reachable.

**Codecs.** Both codecs now render one list of record items instead of the old
opening/user_content/steps split.

- Anthropic: operator items become system messages in the conversation. Clearing ones carry
  `clear_at: "next_user_message"` and the request carries `anthropic-beta:
  mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21`. A clearing and a non-clearing system message
  are never merged. A run of system messages is judged together for placement (after a user
  message, and last or before the assistant's); any run placed elsewhere becomes user text. The
  moving cache breakpoint stays on the newest user message and never goes on a turn-scoped
  system message.
- Responses: operator items become `developer` items, assistant output is inserted verbatim,
  and results become `function_call_output` items followed by user picture messages.

**Skills clear per profile, never per request.** `clears_skills(profile)` is true for the
Anthropic family unless the profile is `account_sign_in` (JusPrin's gateway).

**D5.** `handle_set_chat_model` refuses a model whose format differs from the record's, and
refuses the gateway for a chat whose record has clearing skills. The chat keeps its model, the
page gets its unchanged choice back, and a `bridge_error` with code `chat_format_fixed` says to
start a new chat. A chat with no record takes any model. The same check runs when a turn starts,
because a chat's choice can change under it (for example a provider's key is removed). In that
case the turn fails with the same message.

## Migration of chats from before this change

A chat that talked before this change gets a record the first time it talks again, once. The
record is in that turn's wire format and holds, as plain text only:

- the person's messages and file-load reports up to the last earlier reply that had text;
- the replies.

Earlier tool calls and results, workspace blocks, pictures, skills and notes were never stored,
so they are not made up. Messages after that last reply go as any unsent message does. A chat
with no earlier reply gets no migration.

## Production diff (src/, `0807d77282..HEAD`)

```
 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AgentHost.cpp         | 273 ++++++++++++++-------
 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AgentHost.hpp         |   8 +-
 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AgentService.hpp      |  38 +--
 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AnthropicCodec.cpp    | 153 ++++++------
 .../GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ProjectStateDocument.cpp     | 159 +++++++++++-
 .../GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ProjectStateDocument.hpp     |  76 ++++++
 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ProviderAgent.cpp     | 144 ++++++++---
 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ProviderAgent.hpp     |  27 +-
 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ProviderCodec.hpp     |  73 +-----
 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ProviderProfile.hpp   |  20 ++
 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ResponsesCodec.cpp    |  92 +++----
 .../JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp   |   1 -
 .../GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterPanel.cpp      |   1 -
 13 files changed, 713 insertions(+), 352 deletions(-)
```

Production code grew by 361 lines net, against the brief's aim of shrinking it.

| Commit | Change | Why it grew |
|---|---|---|
| R7 | +599/−327 | The record needs storage and settlement: ProjectStateDocument +226 (types and JSON), ProviderAgent +73 (handing settled items over), AgentHost +51 net (migration and blob I/O, after deleting the rebuild). The codecs and ProviderCodec.hpp shrank by 93. |
| R2 | +70/−28 | The `clears` flag, its storage, the profile rule, and the codec's new message shape. |
| R6 | +32/−23 | The rewritten-note check, and keeping an app turn's workspace together with its note. |
| D5 | +38/−0 | The refusal and the places it is checked. |

Deleted code:

- the host's history rebuild: the calls_by_message replay, the retelling of reports and notes,
  and the stripping of workspace blocks and skills;
- `AgentConversationContext`;
- the transcript's opening/user_content/steps split and the codec paths for it;
- `tool_output_json`;
- `notes_in_context`.

Tests: +917/−325 across 7 files, including the new `tests/agent/kept_turn.hpp` helper.

## Gateway follow-up

JusPrin's gateway sends only the headers it is configured with. Until it passes
`anthropic-beta: mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21`, `account_sign_in` profiles do not
clear skills, so a fired skill stays visible in every later request.

To enable clearing through the gateway:

1. Add the header to the Anthropic alias backend in `JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES` on the server.
2. Make `clears_skills()` in `ProviderProfile.hpp` return true for `account_sign_in` too.
3. Relax D5's gateway refusal in `record_refusal` in `AgentHost.cpp`.

## Every difference in what the model sees

- **Earlier turns.** They are sent exactly as first sent:
  - workspace blocks, attachment listings, pictures and PDFs stay in later requests (they used
    to be stripped);
  - thinking/reasoning and Responses item ids stay;
  - tool calls and results stay in their own channels.
- **Earlier tool results on Anthropic** are `tool_result` content blocks, as within a turn, not a
  plain string.
- **Skills.** A skill stays where it fired.
  - Anthropic direct: hidden after the next user message (`clear_at`).
  - Responses and the gateway: still visible in later requests. Before, a skill was sent once on
    Responses and kept within one turn only on Anthropic.
- **Notes.** Notes are operator messages (Anthropic system, Responses developer) with no
  "JusPrin app note, not the person's words:" prefix. The project chat now sees its notes, which
  it did not before.
  - On Anthropic, a note with nothing from the person before it (a printer chat turn the app
    started) still becomes user text, as the API requires.
  - A note rewritten after it was sent (Undo on a saved-preset receipt) is sent again as it now
    reads.
- **Order within a turn.** Skill pictures, then notes, then skill texts.
- **Stopped or failed responses.** Their partial text and calls are not sent again. A message
  whose turn never reached the model still is.
- **Title requests** send only the person's words, without the chat.
- **Retries** of a turn the record already holds send no new workspace block.
- **Migrated chats.** Earlier words and replies go as plain text. The earlier tool calls that
  used to be replayed are gone.
- **Wire-format switch.** A chat that has talked cannot switch to a model in the other wire
  format, or to the gateway once it has clearing skills. The person has to start a new chat.

## Unverified

- **Anthropic run of system messages.** Unverified whether the Messages API accepts a turn-scoped
  (`clear_at`) system message directly after one that stays. The docs judge a run of system
  messages together but do not say so outright.
- **Responses item ids.** Unverified whether Responses accepts verbatim output items with ids
  (reasoning, message, function_call) from earlier turns when `store:false`. If it rejects them,
  the record must drop ids or keep `encrypted_content`.
- **Wire bytes on a real provider.** No live request was made, so the actual request bytes and
  cache hits were not checked against a real provider. The guard proves byte-identical prefixes
  only against the codecs' own output.
- **Shell harness build.** `tests/shell` and `tests/project_prompt` were not built here (only
  `agent_bridge_tests`). A grep found no use of the removed fields there.
- **Page behaviour on refusal.** The page shows `bridge_error` only as a diagnostic, so after a
  refused model switch the person sees the picker reset without the reason.

## Follow-ups outside this branch's scope

- `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp` (lines ~900, 980, 987, 989): `CalibrationAgent` recognises app
  turns by the old "JusPrin app note, not the person's words:" prefix in `user_text`. It must
  read `request.note` instead, or those harness scenarios stop matching. The sibling session that
  owns `tests/shell` should make this change.
- The Agent page should show `chat_format_fixed` to the person.
- Gateway header and the two code switches, listed under "Gateway follow-up" above.

1. CONFIRMED. Every migrated chat throws on its first request. start_chat_record stores the migrated record with format "" (ProjectStateDocument.cpp:916). ProviderAgent::begin_transcript (ProviderAgent.cpp:239) throws logic_error whenever items are non-empty and format != wire_format(family), so "" fails on both providers, on that message and every later one. The migration test uses RecordingAgent, not ProviderAgent, and asserts the empty format, so it records exactly the input that crashes the real loop. Fix: the migration stamps the turn's wire format (it already knows it), and the test runs the real ProviderAgent with a fake transport over a migrated chat. While there, the same format invariant is checked in three layers (record_refusal in the host, begin_transcript in the agent, append_chat_record in the document); keep the document's check plus the host's refusal and drop the agent's, per AGENTS.md "no duplicated defensive checks".

2. CONFIRMED. The version-store prune deletes every picture and PDF the record keeps. Blobs go to attachments/chat-<conv>/<request>-<n> (ProjectStateDocument.hpp:114, AgentHost.cpp:2766). ProjectVersionStore::prune, run from ProjectAutosave::trim_history after every version, removes every regular file under attachments/ that is not in the document's attachments index (ProjectVersionStore.cpp, final loop). Chat blobs are in neither the index nor live_attachments. Afterwards load_record_bytes gets "" from read_attachment_blob (missing file returns empty) and the next request carries an image block with empty data, permanently, since the record is append-only. Also: a forked managed identity copies only the opened file's attachment folder, so chat blobs are not carried over. Fix: either keep chat blobs somewhere prune never sweeps (own top-level directory in the managed folder, carried on fork and deleted with the chat) or make them part of what prune keeps; and make a missing blob an invariant violation that throws, never an empty picture. Test it through on-disk persistence with the autosave/prune path, not in-memory.

3. CONFIRMED. The record is appended when the transport accepts the post (ProviderAgent.cpp:406, record() right after m_transport->post returns true), not when the provider accepts the request. A 413 or a 400 for a bad or oversized picture then leaves the person's message, workspace block and pictures in the record and the chat can never send again. Fix: append only once the provider has answered 2xx (first stream event or completion), so a rejected request leaves no trace; the "a turn whose request fails" test must distinguish a 503 (message kept, nothing recorded) from a 400/413 (same). Also do the fallible blob write before dispatch, not inside on_recorded after the request is in flight; today an exception there leaves m_busy true with a live request.

Independent review of claude/cache-r7-record-e80b27 found four problems that block merging; three I confirmed by reading your branch. Please fix them on your branch, each with a test that fails first, and report back. Keep the record model; this is a rework of its edges, not a redesign.

1. CONFIRMED. Every migrated chat throws on its first request. start_chat_record stores the migrated record with format "" (ProjectStateDocument.cpp:916). ProviderAgent::begin_transcript (ProviderAgent.cpp:239) throws logic_error whenever items are non-empty and format != wire_format(family), so "" fails on both providers, on that message and every later one. The migration test uses RecordingAgent, not ProviderAgent, and asserts the empty format, so it records exactly the input that crashes the real loop. Fix: the migration stamps the turn's wire format (it already knows it), and the test runs the real ProviderAgent with a fake transport over a migrated chat. While there, the same format invariant is checked in three layers (record_refusal in the host, begin_transcript in the agent, append_chat_record in the document); keep the document's check plus the host's refusal and drop the agent's, per AGENTS.md "no duplicated defensive checks".

2. CONFIRMED. The version-store prune deletes every picture and PDF the record keeps. Blobs go to attachments/chat-<conv>/<request>-<n> (ProjectStateDocument.hpp:114, AgentHost.cpp:2766). ProjectVersionStore::prune, run from ProjectAutosave::trim_history after every version, removes every regular file under attachments/ that is not in the document's attachments index (ProjectVersionStore.cpp, final loop). Chat blobs are in neither the index nor live_attachments. Afterwards load_record_bytes gets "" from read_attachment_blob (missing file returns empty) and the next request carries an image block with empty data, permanently, since the record is append-only. Also: a forked managed identity copies only the opened file's attachment folder, so chat blobs are not carried over. Fix: either keep chat blobs somewhere prune never sweeps (own top-level directory in the managed folder, carried on fork and deleted with the chat) or make them part of what prune keeps; and make a missing blob an invariant violation that throws, never an empty picture. Test it through on-disk persistence with the autosave/prune path, not in-memory.

3. CONFIRMED. The record is appended when the transport accepts the post (ProviderAgent.cpp:406, record() right after m_transport->post returns true), not when the provider accepts the request. A 413 or a 400 for a bad or oversized picture then leaves the person's message, workspace block and pictures in the record and the chat can never send again. Fix: append only once the provider has answered 2xx (first stream event or completion), so a rejected request leaves no trace; the "a turn whose request fails" test must distinguish a 503 (message kept, nothing recorded) from a 400/413 (same). Also do the fallible blob write before dispatch, not inside on_recorded after the request is in flight; today an exception there leaves m_busy true with a live request.

4. UNVERIFIED, needs a live check before merge, which Kenneth has to approve (do not make the call yourself): Responses reasoning items are replayed across turns with their ids under store:false and no encrypted_content (ResponsesCodec.cpp:72-76, :155; no include requested). Community reports describe a 404 "Item … not found. Items are not persisted when store is set to false" for exactly this. If true, the failure is permanent per chat. Read OpenAI's current Responses docs on store:false, reasoning items and include=reasoning.encrypted_content and say what the record must keep for replay to be valid; make the codec change if the docs settle it, and say what a live two-turn check should look for.

Smaller findings, fix if cheap and say which you skipped: retrying a failed reply that is not the newest sends a request ending on an assistant item (make_agent_request early return on empty source, AgentHost.cpp:2967; handle_retry does not require the newest message); turn_recorded re-derives "already sent" from attempt>1 && source.empty() when the host knows it exactly via sent(id); a rewritten note is re-sent only when it starts the turn, and each re-send appends a duplicate id to record.messages (ProjectStateDocument.cpp:902); the record is read leniently (value() defaults, unknown part kinds become PDFs) while written strictly, so read with at() and throw on unknown kinds; a reply request with no on_recorded sink is a silent no-op in record() (ProviderAgent.cpp:329), it should throw; each turn start parses the whole record three times and re-reads and base64-encodes every blob on the GUI thread, parse once per turn and avoid the encode/decode round trip if RecordPart holds bytes.

Growth the reviewer judged unnecessary, about 70-90 production lines: start_record_of_earlier_chat repeats the file-report/user/note if-chain and the report label literal from the unsent loop (merge them); record.messages mostly duplicates the items' source fields (store only the ids the migration covered); the keep lambda and load_record_bytes walk the same parts (one for_each_blob); the host builds AgentUnsentMessage and the agent turns it into RecordItems (hand over ready-made items, which also deletes the test-side copy in kept_turn.hpp that already differs from production: it leaves issue_context untagged where production wraps it in <print_issue>); unreachable fallbacks after exhaustive switches. Do these after the four blockers.

Tests the reviewer found missing: the real ProviderAgent over a migrated record; on-disk persistence through autosave and prune; a 4xx after acceptance and what the next turn sends; a host-level retry after the record holds the message (RetryingAgent never calls on_recorded); a stop or failure followed by a new turn under the history-prefix guard; retrying a failed reply that is not the newest.

Same rules as before: no live calls, commit on your branch, agent suite and guard green, update r7-report.md with what changed and the new production diff stat.

content.content:
**Problem:** With `store=False`, the poster couldn't carry reasoning forward. Passing `reasoning=` as a request parameter was rejected, and appending the reasoning object as a message with a custom role was not allowed. Replaying the reasoning item in `input` without the rest of the output also failed. One user got this error: "of type 'reasoning' was provided without its required following item."

**Resolution:** Add the items from `response.output` to `input` in their original shape, rather than building role-based messages. One user did this with `inputs.extend(response_1.output)` before appending the next user message. The reasoning item must be followed by its paired message item.

**Does `encrypted_content` fix the error?** The thread doesn't establish this. The error was resolved by keeping the reasoning and following message items intact. Whether `encrypted_content` is needed in the replayed item isn't settled. The schema lists it as nullable, and one user said the `include` parameter is optional on the return path, but that claim wasn't tested.

**Keep or strip the `id`?** Keep it. The thread's schema summary lists `id` as required for reasoning input items, and one user reported that exact copies, including IDs, were needed to avoid the error. One commenter speculated that made-up IDs might be tolerated, but this was posed as a question, not confirmed.
