git diff --shortstat -- src; git diff --shortstat -- tests; git add -u src tests && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Keep a chat's record only of what the provider took, and keep its pictures

A review of the chat record found four problems that would break chats in
use. This fixes three of them and settles the fourth from OpenAI's docs.
Each fix has a test that fails without it.

1. Every chat from before the record threw on its first request. The
   migration stored its record with an empty wire format, and the turn loop
   refused any record whose format differed from the provider's. Now the
   host builds the migrated record in memory and stores it together with
   the first items the provider takes, in their format. The loop's own
   format check is gone. The document's check (append_chat_record) and the
   host's refusal of a model in the other format (record_refusal) remain.
   The migration test now runs the real ProviderAgent on both wire
   formats, not a mock.

2. The version store's prune deleted every picture and PDF the record
   kept. Record blobs lived under attachments/, and ProjectVersionStore::
   prune removes every file there that the document's attachment index
   does not name. They now live in a top-level chats/<conversation>/
   folder, which prune never touches. In managed projects too, the folder
   is deleted with its chat, and importing an archive copies it alongside
   attachments/. A blob missing from disk now throws instead of being sent
   as an empty picture on every later request. Blobs hold the base64 text
   exactly as sent, so neither writing nor reading decodes or re-encodes.

3. The record was appended as soon as the transport accepted the post, not
   when the provider accepted the request. A 400 or 413 caused by a bad
   picture then stayed in the record and broke the chat for good. Now
   items join the record at the provider's first stream event, so a
   refused request (503, 400 or 413) leaves no trace and the person's
   message goes again with the next turn. Picture blobs are written before
   the request that first sends them. A blob that cannot be written stops
   the request before it goes out (the turn fails with the existing
   generic error). Before, a failed write threw from the stream callback
   with the request still in flight.

4. Responses reasoning items replayed under store:false. OpenAI's
   reasoning guide (developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/reasoning) says
   that in stateless mode reasoning output items include encrypted_content
   by default. It calls the include value a legacy option that is not
   required, and says to replay output items untouched. The record already
   keeps them verbatim, ids included, so the codec is unchanged. Only a
   live two-turn check can confirm this.

Smaller fixes:
- Only the chat's last reply can be retried. Retrying an earlier failed
  reply sent a request ending on an assistant item.
- AgentRequest::turn_recorded is set by the host, which knows it, instead
  of being re-derived from attempt and source.
- A rewritten note is sent again whichever turn comes next, not only when
  it starts the turn. The record no longer keeps a list of message ids,
  so a resend no longer adds a duplicate id: ChatRecord::holds() looks at
  the items' sources plus the ids a migration covered.
- The record is read strictly. Fields use at(), and an unknown part or
  item kind throws.
- A reply request with no record sink is a logic error. AgentSetup's key
  check is not a chat, so it passes no-op sinks.
- A turn start reads the record once, not three times.

Trimmed: the host hands the loop ready-made RecordItems for unsent
messages (AgentUnsentMessage is gone, and the test helper now tags print
issues as production does). The migration and the unsent loop share one
message-to-item function. The record-kind name fallback and the codecs'
unreachable switch fallbacks are gone.

What the model sees that is new: when a later request of a turn is
refused or fails, that turn's calls and results are no longer kept. The
next turn sees the person's message and the current workspace, not the
calls the model made.

Not verified: the real prune. ProjectVersionStore needs libslic3r, which
is not built in this worktree, so the managed-project test applies prune's
rule for attachments/ itself. No live request was made.

Production diff of this commit: +274/-226 (net +48).
EOF

# R7: every chat sends an append-only record of what it sent

Each request a chat sends now starts with the exact bytes of its previous request, so the
provider's prompt cache can reuse the earlier part on Anthropic Messages and OpenAI Responses.

A review found four blocking problems. Three are fixed in `17300104a0`, each with a test that
fails without its fix. The fourth (Responses reasoning items) is settled from OpenAI's current
docs, but needs a live check that Kenneth must approve.

Test results:

- Agent suite: 17152 assertions in 486 test cases, random order.
- History-prefix guard: 178 assertions in 4 test cases, on both wire formats.
- No live model calls were made.

The work is on branch `claude/cache-r7-record-e80b27`: six commits on `0807d77282`. Nothing is
pushed or merged.

| Commit | What |
|---|---|
| `ba08e2c18f` | R7: the per-chat record replaces the rebuilt history |
| `fe70eea593` | R2: a fired skill clears at the next user message on Anthropic (not through the gateway) |
| `f5039d09e8` | R6: app notes are operator messages in project and printer chats |
| `59304a1ef9` | D5: a chat that has talked refuses a model in the other wire format |
| `9fce6ddb2b` | The `[history-prefix]` guard runs by default (test-only) |
| `17300104a0` | Review fixes: record only what the provider took, keep pictures out of prune's reach, stamp the migration's format |

The `17300104a0` message gives that commit's production diff as "+274/-226". The real figure is
+267/−219; the net +48 is correct. The commit was not amended, because the git policy requires
confirmation first.

## Design as built

### The record

`ProjectStateDocument` keeps a `ChatRecord` per chat with three fields:

- `format`: `"anthropic"` or `"responses"`. It is fixed by the first stored items and never empty.
- `items`: everything the chat sent, in order.
- `migrated`: the message ids a migration covered (see below).

Each `RecordItem` is one of four kinds:

- `User`: the person's message as sent (words, a `<print_issue>` block, the workspace block, the
  attachment listing, pictures and PDFs). Its `source` is the message id.
- `Operator`: a fired skill's text or an app note. `clears` is set on skills the provider can hide
  later (R2).
- `Assistant`: the provider's output exactly as returned, thinking or reasoning included. Responses
  items keep their ids.
- `Results`: tool results, in the provider's tool-result channel, pictures included.

`ChatRecord::holds(id)` answers "was this message sent?" from the items' sources plus the
`migrated` ids. The record is read strictly: missing fields and unknown kinds throw. Items are only
appended, and `append_chat_record` checks everything before it changes anything.

### Pictures and PDFs

These are stored as blobs under `chats/<conversation>/<request_id>-<n>`, relative to the JusPrin
data dir. Each blob holds the base64 text exactly as sent, so neither writing nor reading decodes
or re-encodes. state.json stores only the blob paths.

The folder is a top-level `chats/`, not under `attachments/`. `ProjectVersionStore::prune` removes
every file under `attachments/` that the document's attachment index does not name. Prune runs
after every version (from `ProjectAutosave::trim_history`) and never reads chat records.

The folder is deleted with its chat, in managed projects too: `remove_attachment_dir` still skips
`attachments/` folders there, because published versions can reference them. Importing an archive
copies `chats/` alongside `attachments/`. A blob missing when a turn starts throws a
`RuntimeError`, instead of sending an empty picture on every later request.

### When items join the record

`ProviderAgent` hands items to `AgentRequest::on_recorded` at the provider's first stream event for
a request, when everything before `m_settled` is appended.

- A request the provider refuses (503, 400, 413, or any transport error) leaves nothing behind.
- Within a turn, items settle at these points:
  - the person's side, once its request is taken;
  - a response together with its results, once the next request is taken;
  - the final response, at completion.
- A trailing operator item (a skill or note) and a call without its result are never stored.
- In an app turn (one started by a note), the turn's workspace item and the note are settled
  together.

Each picture's blob is written through `AgentRequest::keep_blob` before the request that first
sends it. If a blob cannot be written, the request is never sent and the turn fails with the
existing generic error. A reply request with no sinks is a `logic_error`. `AgentSetup`'s key check
is not a chat, so it passes no-op sinks.

### Request order

Each request is built in this order:

1. the record;
2. the person's messages not yet sent;
3. the turn's own user item (with no source in an app turn);
4. fired skills' pictures;
5. notes (unsent notes, then the turn's note);
6. fired skills' texts.

The host hands the loop ready-made `RecordItem`s for unsent messages. The host also sets
`turn_recorded` when the record already holds the turn's message (a retry); the loop then adds no
new workspace block. The migration and the unsent loop share one message-to-item function
(`as_sent`).

### Codecs

- Anthropic: operator items become system messages. Clearing ones carry
  `clear_at: "next_user_message"`, and the request carries the header
  `anthropic-beta: mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21`. Placement is judged per run of
  system messages, and a misplaced run becomes user text.
- Responses: operator items become `developer` items, output is replayed verbatim, and results are
  `function_call_output` items followed by user messages with the pictures.

### D5: switching wire formats

`set_chat_model` refuses a model whose format differs from the record's. It also refuses the
gateway for a chat whose record holds clearing skills. The refusal sends `chat_format_fixed` as a
`bridge_error`. The same check runs at turn start, against the record read once for that turn.

### Retry

Only the chat's last reply can be retried. Retrying an earlier failed reply now gets
`invalid_retry`. Before, it sent a request that ended on an assistant item.

## Migration of chats from before the record

The first turn of an older chat builds its record in memory from the messages up to the last
earlier reply with text, as plain text:

- the person's words, with a `<print_issue>` block where the message had one;
- file-load reports;
- the replies.

Notes, calls, results, workspace blocks and pictures were never stored, so they are not made up.
The covered ids go into `migrated`. Messages after the last reply go as any unsent message does.

The migrated record is stored together with the first items the provider takes, in the format of
that request. This fixed the bug where every migrated chat threw on its first request: the old
migration stored format `""`, and the loop refused any record whose format differed from the
provider's.

The migration test now runs the real `ProviderAgent` on both wire formats, and checks two things:

- the earlier words go exactly once;
- the next turn opens with the migrated turn's request.

## Responses reasoning items under store:false (blocker 4)

OpenAI's reasoning guide (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/reasoning, read
2026-10-29) states three things:

- In stateless mode (`store:false` or Zero Data Retention), reasoning items in a response's
  `output` "include an `encrypted_content` property by default".
- The `include` value `reasoning.encrypted_content` is a legacy value, still accepted "for
  compatibility, but doesn't require it".
- Items should be passed into the next request "untouched", and the complete history replayed.

For replay to be valid, the record must keep every output item exactly as returned: the reasoning
item with its `id` and `encrypted_content`, the message items (with any `phase`), and the
`function_call` items. It already does, so the codec is unchanged. I did not add `include`, because
JusPrin's gateway refuses fields it does not list.

The 404 "Items are not persisted when store is set to false" reported on community.openai.com
matches a reasoning item replayed without `encrypted_content`. Under the current docs that should
not happen.

The live check needs Kenneth's approval. It is a two-turn chat on a reasoning model with `effort`
set, through the app, on OpenAI directly, and if possible also through OpenRouter and the gateway.
It should confirm three things:

1. Turn 1's response holds a `reasoning` item with a non-null `encrypted_content`.
2. Turn 2's request carries that item byte for byte.
3. Turn 2 succeeds with no 404 and no "Item … not found". Ideally `cached_tokens` is above zero.

The same replay already happened within a turn before R7, whenever a tool call was followed by its
result.

## Every difference in what the model sees

- **Earlier turns** are sent exactly as first sent:
  - workspace blocks, attachment listings, pictures and PDFs stay in later requests (they used to
    be stripped);
  - thinking or reasoning stays, and Responses items keep their ids;
  - tool calls and results stay in their own channels.
- **Earlier tool results on Anthropic** are `tool_result` content blocks, not a plain string.
- **Skills** stay where they fired:
  - straight to Anthropic, the provider hides them after the next user message;
  - on Responses and through the gateway, they stay visible.
- **Notes** are operator messages (Anthropic system, Responses developer) with no "JusPrin app
  note…" prefix. The project chat now sees its notes, which it did not see before. A note rewritten
  after it was sent (Undo on a receipt) goes again as it now reads, whichever turn comes next.
- **Order within a turn**: skill pictures, then notes, then skill texts.
- **Refused or failed requests** (new in the review fixes):
  - A refused request leaves nothing behind, and the person's message goes again with the next
    turn.
  - When a later request of a turn is refused or fails, the calls the model made in that turn are
    not stored. The next turn sees the person's message and the current workspace, not those
    calls.
  - A stopped or failed response's partial text is not sent again.
- **Retries**:
  - A retry after the provider took the turn's request sends that request again, byte for byte.
  - Only the chat's last reply can be retried.
- **Title requests** send only the person's words.
- **Migrated chats**: earlier words and replies go once, as plain text, with any print-issue block.
- **Format switch**: a chat that has talked cannot switch to a model in the other wire format, or
  to the gateway once it has clearing skills.

- **The real prune.** `ProjectVersionStore` and `ProjectAutosave` need libslic3r and the GUI
  library, which are not built in this worktree (258 compiles). The managed-project test applies
  prune's rule for `attachments/` itself, copied from `ProjectVersionStore.cpp`'s final loop.
- **Exported archives.** Unverified whether an exported archive from a managed project carries
  `chats/`. Import copies `chats/` when the archive's auxiliary folder has it.
- **Anthropic system-message runs.** Unverified whether the Messages API accepts a turn-scoped
  (`clear_at`) system message directly after one that stays.
- **Responses replay.** Unverified live (see above).
- **Anthropic merged user messages.** When a turn's later request is refused, the record ends on
  the person's side, and Anthropic merges the next turn's user message into it. The guard compares
  that case by content block, on the documented basis that Anthropic caches by block. A live cache
  hit for it is unverified.
- **Other test targets.** `tests/shell`, `tests/project_prompt` and `agent_live_tests` were not
  built. `test_provider_live.cpp` got the record sinks by text edit only.
- **No live requests** were made at any point.

  note…" prefix in `user_text`. It must read `request.note`. That folder belongs to the sibling
  session; a note was left in the shared notes folder.
- The Agent page shows `bridge_error` only as a diagnostic. The person should be told about
  `chat_format_fixed`, and about `invalid_retry` for an earlier reply. Before this branch the page
  may also offer Retry on earlier failed replies; unverified.
- **Gateway clearing.** To let skills clear through the gateway:
  1. Add the `anthropic-beta: mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21` header to the Anthropic
     alias backend in `JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES`.
  2. Make `clears_skills()` return true for `account_sign_in` profiles.
  3. Relax the gateway refusal in `record_refusal`.

# R7: every chat sends an append-only record of what it sent

Each request a chat sends now starts with the exact bytes of its previous request, so the
provider's prompt cache can reuse the earlier part on Anthropic Messages and OpenAI Responses.

A review found four blocking problems. Three are fixed in `17300104a0`, each with a test that
fails without its fix. The fourth (Responses reasoning items) is settled from OpenAI's current
docs, but needs a live check that Kenneth must approve.

Test results:

- Agent suite: 17152 assertions in 486 test cases, random order.
- History-prefix guard: 178 assertions in 4 test cases, on both wire formats.
- No live model calls were made.

The work is on branch `claude/cache-r7-record-e80b27`: six commits on `0807d77282`. Nothing is
pushed or merged.

| Commit | What |
|---|---|
| `ba08e2c18f` | R7: the per-chat record replaces the rebuilt history |
| `fe70eea593` | R2: a fired skill clears at the next user message on Anthropic (not through the gateway) |
| `f5039d09e8` | R6: app notes are operator messages in project and printer chats |
| `59304a1ef9` | D5: a chat that has talked refuses a model in the other wire format |
| `9fce6ddb2b` | The `[history-prefix]` guard runs by default (test-only) |
| `17300104a0` | Review fixes: record only what the provider took, keep pictures out of prune's reach, stamp the migration's format |

The `17300104a0` message gives that commit's production diff as "+274/-226". The real figure is
+267/−219; the net +48 is correct. The commit was not amended, because the git policy requires
confirmation first.

## Design as built

### The record

`ProjectStateDocument` keeps a `ChatRecord` per chat with three fields:

- `format`: `"anthropic"` or `"responses"`. It is fixed by the first stored items and never empty.
- `items`: everything the chat sent, in order.
- `migrated`: the message ids a migration covered (see below).

Each `RecordItem` is one of four kinds:

- `User`: the person's message as sent (words, a `<print_issue>` block, the workspace block, the
  attachment listing, pictures and PDFs). Its `source` is the message id.
- `Operator`: a fired skill's text or an app note. `clears` is set on skills the provider can hide
  later (R2).
- `Assistant`: the provider's output exactly as returned, thinking or reasoning included. Responses
  items keep their ids.
- `Results`: tool results, in the provider's tool-result channel, pictures included.

`ChatRecord::holds(id)` answers "was this message sent?" from the items' sources plus the
`migrated` ids. The record is read strictly: missing fields and unknown kinds throw. Items are only
appended, and `append_chat_record` checks everything before it changes anything.

### Pictures and PDFs

These are stored as blobs under `chats/<conversation>/<request_id>-<n>`, relative to the JusPrin
data dir. Each blob holds the base64 text exactly as sent, so neither writing nor reading decodes
or re-encodes. state.json stores only the blob paths.

The folder is a top-level `chats/`, not under `attachments/`. `ProjectVersionStore::prune` removes
every file under `attachments/` that the document's attachment index does not name. Prune runs
after every version (from `ProjectAutosave::trim_history`) and never reads chat records.

The folder is deleted with its chat, in managed projects too: `remove_attachment_dir` still skips
`attachments/` folders there, because published versions can reference them. Importing an archive
copies `chats/` alongside `attachments/`. A blob missing when a turn starts throws a
`RuntimeError`, instead of sending an empty picture on every later request.

### When items join the record

`ProviderAgent` hands items to `AgentRequest::on_recorded` at the provider's first stream event for
a request, when everything before `m_settled` is appended.

- A request the provider refuses (503, 400, 413, or any transport error) leaves nothing behind.
- Within a turn, items settle at these points:
  - the person's side, once its request is taken;
  - a response together with its results, once the next request is taken;
  - the final response, at completion.
- A trailing operator item (a skill or note) and a call without its result are never stored.
- In an app turn (one started by a note), the turn's workspace item and the note are settled
  together.

Each picture's blob is written through `AgentRequest::keep_blob` before the request that first
sends it. If a blob cannot be written, the request is never sent and the turn fails with the
existing generic error. A reply request with no sinks is a `logic_error`. `AgentSetup`'s key check
is not a chat, so it passes no-op sinks.

### Request order

Each request is built in this order:

1. the record;
2. the person's messages not yet sent;
3. the turn's own user item (with no source in an app turn);
4. fired skills' pictures;
5. notes (unsent notes, then the turn's note);
6. fired skills' texts.

The host hands the loop ready-made `RecordItem`s for unsent messages. The host also sets
`turn_recorded` when the record already holds the turn's message (a retry); the loop then adds no
new workspace block. The migration and the unsent loop share one message-to-item function
(`as_sent`).

### Codecs

- Anthropic: operator items become system messages. Clearing ones carry
  `clear_at: "next_user_message"`, and the request carries the header
  `anthropic-beta: mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21`. Placement is judged per run of
  system messages, and a misplaced run becomes user text.
- Responses: operator items become `developer` items, output is replayed verbatim, and results are
  `function_call_output` items followed by user messages with the pictures.

### D5: switching wire formats

`set_chat_model` refuses a model whose format differs from the record's. It also refuses the
gateway for a chat whose record holds clearing skills. The refusal sends `chat_format_fixed` as a
`bridge_error`. The same check runs at turn start, against the record read once for that turn.

### Retry

Only the chat's last reply can be retried. Retrying an earlier failed reply now gets
`invalid_retry`. Before, it sent a request that ended on an assistant item.

## Migration of chats from before the record

The first turn of an older chat builds its record in memory from the messages up to the last
earlier reply with text, as plain text:

- the person's words, with a `<print_issue>` block where the message had one;
- file-load reports;
- the replies.

Notes, calls, results, workspace blocks and pictures were never stored, so they are not made up.
The covered ids go into `migrated`. Messages after the last reply go as any unsent message does.

The migrated record is stored together with the first items the provider takes, in the format of
that request. This fixed the bug where every migrated chat threw on its first request: the old
migration stored format `""`, and the loop refused any record whose format differed from the
provider's.

The migration test now runs the real `ProviderAgent` on both wire formats, and checks two things:

- the earlier words go exactly once;
- the next turn opens with the migrated turn's request.

## Responses reasoning items under store:false (blocker 4)

OpenAI's reasoning guide (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/reasoning, read
2026-10-29) states three things:

- In stateless mode (`store:false` or Zero Data Retention), reasoning items in a response's
  `output` "include an `encrypted_content` property by default".
- The `include` value `reasoning.encrypted_content` is a legacy value, still accepted "for
  compatibility, but doesn't require it".
- Items should be passed into the next request "untouched", and the complete history replayed.

For replay to be valid, the record must keep every output item exactly as returned: the reasoning
item with its `id` and `encrypted_content`, the message items (with any `phase`), and the
`function_call` items. It already does, so the codec is unchanged. I did not add `include`, because
JusPrin's gateway refuses fields it does not list.

The 404 "Items are not persisted when store is set to false" reported on community.openai.com
matches a reasoning item replayed without `encrypted_content`. Under the current docs that should
not happen.

The live check needs Kenneth's approval. It is a two-turn chat on a reasoning model with `effort`
set, through the app, on OpenAI directly, and if possible also through OpenRouter and the gateway.
It should confirm three things:

1. Turn 1's response holds a `reasoning` item with a non-null `encrypted_content`.
2. Turn 2's request carries that item byte for byte.
3. Turn 2 succeeds with no 404 and no "Item … not found". Ideally `cached_tokens` is above zero.

The same replay already happened within a turn before R7, whenever a tool call was followed by its
result.

## Every difference in what the model sees

- **Earlier turns** are sent exactly as first sent:
  - workspace blocks, attachment listings, pictures and PDFs stay in later requests (they used to
    be stripped);
  - thinking or reasoning stays, and Responses items keep their ids;
  - tool calls and results stay in their own channels.
- **Earlier tool results on Anthropic** are `tool_result` content blocks, not a plain string.
- **Skills** stay where they fired:
  - straight to Anthropic, the provider hides them after the next user message;
  - on Responses and through the gateway, they stay visible.
- **Notes** are operator messages (Anthropic system, Responses developer) with no "JusPrin app
  note…" prefix. The project chat now sees its notes, which it did not see before. A note rewritten
  after it was sent (Undo on a receipt) goes again as it now reads, whichever turn comes next.
- **Order within a turn**: skill pictures, then notes, then skill texts.
- **Refused or failed requests** (new in the review fixes):
  - A refused request leaves nothing behind, and the person's message goes again with the next
    turn.
  - When a later request of a turn is refused or fails, the calls the model made in that turn are
    not stored. The next turn sees the person's message and the current workspace, not those
    calls.
  - A stopped or failed response's partial text is not sent again.
- **Retries**:

  - Only the chat's last reply can be retried.

- **Migrated chats**: earlier words and replies go once, as plain text, with any print-issue block.
